answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work gates registration: each applicant solves a puzzle forcing random reads over gigabytes of state, so speed is capped by memory bandwidth, not cores. Forging a thousand identities means buying a thousand banks of real RAM, priced like ferrous ingots, not copied free. Proofs embed chip latency fingerprints, so cloned hardware clones the tell. Difficulty retargets each epoch, slow as a glacier, keeping cost stable, while honest reputation grows in dense cedar rings. Attackers pay continuously in power and hardware for identities that earn nothing until established.
